reason: The proposed model changes the bag information bottleneck from one latent location/extreme vector to a fixed multi-statistic description of latent location, dispersion, tails, and extremes. This directly tests the distribution-preservation mechanism implicated by Stages 16, 19, 22, and the Stage 24B gap. The novelty is limited because FULL_48 already performs human-specified distributional aggregation, chronology and persistence remain incompletely represented, and a positive result could otherwise be dismissed as a higher-dimensional customer representation or HGB effect. One bounded classifier-matched experiment with a direct-distribution control is defensible; unconstrained architecture escalation is not.
exact_hypothesis: Customer-level theft discrimination depends partly on across-window location, dispersion, tail, and extreme structure that a single mean, maximum, or attention-weighted latent vector cannot preserve; under the same SUMMARY_17 input and Stage 24B encoder, fixed multi-statistic pooling of learned latent dimensions will improve customer discrimination, and a classifier-matched direct-distribution control will determine whether any gain is attributable to learned latent behaviours rather than distribution pooling alone.
chronology_decision: Remain permutation invariant; explicitly accept inability to recover FULL_48 late-third-minus-early-third contrasts.
